lines.meet: I'm Elias, a sun cleric, and I stand in front. Take your time, I've got this side. Sorry if I'm in your way, I'm a big man.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're on this coast too, near the Drownbell? I've seen you on the sand. I'm Elias, and I'm building a shelter down the beach.
lines.ask_home: So where's home for you, {hermano|hermana}? I like to know where people's people are.
lines.ask_work: What did you work at back home, mi pana? Tell me, take your time.
lines.answer_home: Santo Domingo, with a big family, a loud city, and my grandmother's church every Sunday.
lines.answer_work: I fixed motorbikes for twelve years with my cousin, in a workshop with a tin roof. We argued about the radio every single day.
lines.chat_food: My grandmother's sancocho, {hermano|hermana}, with everything in it. On a Sunday after church, it fixed whatever was wrong with you.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep fine, mostly. I check on everybody before I lie down, though, with my little mirror, and that takes a while.
lines.chat_missing: Bachata on a bad radio, while my cousin and I argued over a bike. One more afternoon of that would do me a lot of good.
lines.chat_here: The Light showed up while I was fixing a cart, in my second year. Nothing special happened, it was just there. I treat it like any new tool and learn what it can take.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you're so quiet, I keep checking on you in my mirror. Make a little noise for me.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, you'd talk the paint off a bike, mi pana. My cousin was the same, and I loved him for it.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you check everything twice, like a good mechanic. I'd let you work on my bike, and I don't let anybody.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, you ride like there's no such thing as brakes. I'll be right behind you, fixing what falls off.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you're like an old bike that runs on stubbornness. I mean that as a compliment, {hermano|hermana}.
lines.tease_back: Ha, you got me there, {name}. That's fair enough, mi pana.
lines.take_it_kindly: My grandmother would've said the same, {name}. I won't argue.
lines.bristle: Not that one, {name}, please. Some things I keep in the toolbox.
lines.apologise: I'm sorry, that wasn't kind of me. I'm not usually like that.
lines.double_down: I'm keeping that one, mi pana. Somebody needed to say it gently, and I tried.
lines.needle_quiet: You don't tell anybody when something's wrong. I can only fix what I can see.
lines.needle_talker: You talk over everybody, {hermano|hermana}. Give the others a turn, please.
lines.needle_careful: You take it apart and never put it back together. At some point you have to try the engine.
lines.needle_bold: You rush every repair. A bike you rush breaks down on the road, every time.
lines.needle_any: You make a big show of everything, and it gets in the way of the work.
lines.bite_back: I've stood in front of you every fight, and I didn't complain once. Don't tell me I'm not doing my part.
lines.hurt: That's maybe fair, mi pana. I'll have to take it apart later and see.
lines.laugh_off: My cousin said worse to me every morning for twelve years, mi pana. You'll have to try harder.
lines.confide: {name}, everybody says I coped well with all this. I'm not sure I've got to it properly yet, and I think it's still waiting for me somewhere.
lines.listen: I'm glad you told me, {name}. Sit with me, there's no hurry at all.
lines.look_out: I've got your side in there, {name}, like always, so keep close.
lines.accept: You know best this time, {name}, I'll follow.
lines.deflect: I'm fine, {name}, I'm fine. Look after the others, I'm built for this.
lines.check_in: {name}, let me see you. Where did it get you?
lines.blame: Somebody rushed it, and the whole thing came apart. It wasn't me, mi pana.
lines.thank: Mi pana, I felt the Light go out and you lit it again. Gracias, from my heart.
lines.brush_off: It's what we do, mi pana. Rest a minute.
lines.worry: {name}, I saw that in my mirror and I didn't like it. Sit down a minute, please.
lines.handed_down: Mi pana, I think this was yours. I'll keep it running for you.
lines.hand_fine: Keep it, {hermano|hermana}, it suits you. I've got my mirror, that's enough.
lines.hand_sulk: I'd have handed it over if someone had asked. Nobody asked me, though.
lines.turn_friendly: Mi pana {name}, you're good people. I'm glad you're on my side.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, if I ever build a workshop here, you've got a bench in it, mi pana. Family gets a bench.
lines.turn_grating: We don't run smooth together, do we? That's okay, we'll find a way.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still stand in front of you, because that's what I do. That's all it is, though.
lines.make_up: {name}, this has gone on long enough, mi pana. Let's tune it up and start again.
lines.defend: Easy, now, that's not fair. Leave {name} out of it.
lines.friend_left: My mirror keeps showing an empty space where {name} used to be.
lines.friend_back: {name}, good to see you, mi pana! Your side's still free.
lines.common_machines: Twelve years under motorbikes in a tin-roofed workshop, and I could hear a bad chain from across the street. You know engines too, mi pana.
lines.common_faith: My grandmother took me to church every Sunday, and when she couldn't ask any more, I kept going because I liked the singing. I don't make a show of it.
lines.common_spanish: Ah, you speak Spanish! Mi pana, talk to me, I've been rationing my English all week.
